### Halo Wars (`hw1`)

Written in batch R4 preparation, before any `hw1` unit is coded, from the 2009 manual and the Xbox.com quick reference chart (both Microsoft PDFs, hosted by Halopedia), Halopedia's Halo Wars building tables, its word-for-word copies of the official site's unit pages, and the Definitive Edition's game data (`squads.xml`).

- **Designation: the in-game role line.** The game gives every unit a short role text, and in the game data each squad points to it with a `RoleTextID`. Halopedia's Halo Wars building tables give that line in their Type column and the unit's rollover text in their Description column. Evidence that both columns are game text: the building rows repeat, word for word, the quotes Halopedia marks as in-game descriptions on the buildings' own pages (Warehouse, Temple), and the `RoleTextID` of every unit in the Definitive Edition's `squads.xml` decodes, through Halo Wars 2's legacy string table (which kept the first game's ids), to the same words as the Type column.
  - Read it on these pages, cited as kind wiki with a note that the Type and Description columns copy the in-game text: https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Barracks, https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Vehicle_Depot, https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Airpad, https://www.halopedia.org/Firebase (Warthog and the leader units Elephant, Cyclops, Gremlin), https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Citadel (Scarab, Suicide Grunts, Brutes, Elite Honor Guard), https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Hall, https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Factory, https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Summit and https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Temple (the three Covenant leaders).
  - The lines: Main Infantry (Marines, ODSTs, Grunt squad), Main Vehicle (Scorpion, Grizzly, Wraith), Main Air (Hornet, Hawk, Banshee), Anti-Infantry (Flamethrower, Jackal), Anti-Vehicle (Cobra, Hunter), Anti-Air (Wolverine, Vampire), Scout (Warthog, Ghost, Brute Chopper), Building Killer (Cyclops, Locust), Combat Support (Gremlin), Support Unit (Engineer), Mobile Mini-Base (Elephant), Special Forces (Spartan, Brutes, Elite Honor Guard, Suicide Grunts), Uber Unit (Vulture, Scarab), Leader (Arbiter, Brute Chieftain, Prophet of Regret).
  - Every unit has a role line, so step 1 never falls back to a one-line description.
- **Roles step 1: which lines name a role.**
  - Anti-Infantry: anti-infantry. Anti-Vehicle: anti-armour (its alias). Anti-Air: anti-air. Scout: scout. Support Unit: support, which the Engineer meets (it repairs and heals).
  - Combat Support names support in a word form, but the Gremlin neither repairs nor resupplies, so step 1 skips support (as the RA3 note does for Field Support) and goes on.
  - These name no role: Main Infantry, Main Vehicle, Main Air, Building Killer (no label or alias of ours; it is not siege), Mobile Mini-Base, Special Forces, Uber Unit, Leader.
  - Troop Transport (a transport alias) belongs only to the Pelican and Spirit dropships in the data, which no building's list in the manual or on Halopedia offers: they are not researched.
- **Other official text.** It never replaces the role line at step 1, but it counts for roles.secondary step 1 (a label or alias anywhere in it, in any word form), for strong-against wording at roles.primary step 4 and roles.secondary step 3, and for the weak-point rule that drops a secondary role.
  - **The manual** (Microsoft's 2009 PDF; Halopedia hosts a copy at https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/4/4d/HW_Manual.pdf, from its page https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_manual, which also names the original download.microsoft.com address). Each unit entry gives the building, the required tech level, a sentence or two on the unit, its starting special attack and its upgrades: UNSC units on PDF pages 14 to 17, Covenant leaders on 17 and 18, Covenant units on 21 to 23. Cite it as kind official.
  - **The quick reference chart** (Xbox.com, 2009; Halopedia's copy https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/9/91/HW_TechTree.pdf, from https://www.halopedia.org/File:HW_TechTree.pdf). Four sheets giving every unit, building and upgrade a tech level and a short phrase. Kind official.
  - **The official site's unit pages.** halowars.com is gone; Halopedia copies its pages word for word at https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/UNSC and https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/Covenant. Cite those as kind wiki with a note naming the original site. Nine units there have a Role line: Marines (all purpose), Flamethrower (anti-infantry), Spartan (special forces), Scorpion (main battle tank), Wolverine (anti-air), Cobra (anti-armor), Hornet (antipersonnel), Ghost (scouting) and Engineer (healing). So the Hornet's antipersonnel and the Engineer's healing name anti-infantry and support for roles.secondary step 1, and the Ghost's scouting names scout. The pages were written around the 2009 launch and miss the three Covenant leaders and every leader's own unit (Elephant, ODSTs, Cyclops, Grizzly, Gremlin, Hawk, Suicide Grunts, Brutes, Brute Chopper, Elite Honor Guard).
  - **The rollover texts** in Halopedia's Description column.
  - Not official: Halopedia's own prose, its Tactics and Strategy sections, the unit infobox's role field (the Type-25 Wraith page calls it an artillery tank: the wiki's words), and the leader gameplay pages.
- **Strong-against and weak-against.** No Strong vs or Weak vs lines exist. Read these, in this order of weight:
  1. **The manual's triangle** (PDF page 7, Unit Types). It says there are three kinds of mainline unit and each beats one other kind: vehicles beat infantry, infantry beats aircraft, aircraft beat vehicles; units with specialised jobs are left to their own entries. It is official strong-against text for the mainline units only: those whose role line is Main Infantry, Main Vehicle or Main Air (the manual and the chart call the same units mainline or main). So Marines, ODSTs and Grunts are strong against air; the Scorpion, Grizzly and Wraith against infantry; the Hornet, Hawk and Banshee against vehicles, which means armour.
  2. **Each unit's own wording.** The manual and chart call some units counter-infantry, counter-vehicle, counter-air or counter-building: that is strong-against wording for infantry, armour, air and structures (structures give no anti role); it is not a role label, so it adds nothing at roles.secondary step 1. The rollover texts and the site's prose say the same in other words: the Flamethrower is best at killing infantry, the Cobra is a strong threat to vehicles, the Wolverine is very effective against air units, the Hunter is a danger even to tanks, and the Wraith can wreck lines of armour and groups of infantry from afar. Weak wording: the Gremlin's rollover says it is less effective against infantry, and the site says the Wolverine is vulnerable to anti-armour attacks (an armour class, not a target kind: no role to drop).
  3. Words that name no single kind give nothing: the Marines' rollover (good against nearly everything), the Vulture's manual entry (good against everything) and the Scarab's (all classes of target).
  - Target words: infantry, troops, soldiers and organic targets mean infantry; vehicles, tanks and armour mean armour; air, aircraft and air units mean air; buildings, bases and structures match no anti role.
- **Bonus from the game data (roles step 4).** The Definitive Edition's damage table (`weapontypes.xml`) gives every weapon type a multiplier against each target category, and each weapon's type is in its unit's tactics file (see the research notes for the addresses). A multiplier above 1 counts as extra damage, by step 4's clause on resist tables. Read the categories as kinds: Light, LightArmored and CovenantLeader are infantry, Medium and Heavy are armour, MediumAir is air; Building, Shielded (worn by infantry, vehicles and a leader alike) and Flood name no kind. Where the categories of one kind differ, use the largest. Examples: SmallArms (the Marines' rifle) is above 1 against the three infantry categories, Medium and Shielded, with the largest against Light; AntiAir is far above 1 against MediumAir; ArmorPiercing against Medium and Heavy; Explosive (the Scorpion's and Wraith's main guns) is a little above 1 against everything but MediumAir and Shielded, highest against Medium and Heavy. Both this and the official text count; then step 4's tie rule and each role's requires decide (an Explosive main gun fails anti-armour's requires under the damage map, so the Scorpion's armour bonus is skipped and its infantry bonus, which the triangle backs, remains).
- **Sides and leaders.** Text about one leader's version of a unit counts only for that version. Where a unit is recorded once for its side although a leader changes it (the Brute Chieftain's Grunt squads are led by a Brute, the others' by an Elite), read only the text that every version shares.
notes.game_wide:
### Halo Wars (`hw1`)

Written in batch R4 preparation, before any `hw1` unit is coded, from the 2009 manual (PDF pages 6 to 23), the quick reference chart, Halopedia's Halo Wars, Resources, Leader power, Heal and Repair, HW:Control schemes, Boarding (gameplay mechanic), Active camouflage, building and neutral-structure pages, Halo Nation's Standard (Halo Wars), Deathmatch (Halo Wars) and Supplies pages, and the Definitive Edition's game data (addresses under the research notes). Halopedia pages are https://www.halopedia.org/<Title>, read through the API.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): select, move, attack, cancel, rally points, control groups and camera moves. The attack button also gathers. Units open fire by themselves on enemies near them or on attackers (manual, PDF page 6; HW:Control schemes, both control lists). Neither control list nor the manual has stances, attack-move, patrol, a retreat or a reinforce order. Leave them off.
  - The special attack (Y on the controller, R on PC) is not a basic order: each unit has its own, with a recharge timer, and pressing it fires the specials of every selected unit (manual, PDF page 6). Record it on the unit.
- **Veterancy** (`earn-veterancy`): every unit earns up to three stars by fighting, and each star raises its attack, rate of fire, defence and health (Halo Wars page, Game concepts, Veterancy points). In the game data every unit read has three ranks, each with its own experience threshold, each cutting the damage the unit takes and raising the damage it deals (`objects.xml`, the Veterancy lines). Leave it off every unit.
  - The same Halopedia section says stars also come from upgrading the unit. In the game data each unit upgrade raises a level stored on the squad as well as its numbers. Treat that as the upgrade, not as rank (see Unit upgrades).
  - A vehicle a Spartan has boarded can climb past three (the same section gives the counts). That belongs to the Spartan's boarding (see Spartans and vehicles), not to the vehicle.
  - The Engineer's thresholds are all zero in the data and it has no weapon: whether it ranks at all is unclear. Add an uncertain entry if it matters.
- **Unit upgrades** (`upgrade-in-field` where they add a weapon or a button): every unit has up to three upgrades, bought once at the building that makes it (Halo Nation's Standard page; the manual's unit entries). The in-game texts say they reach all units of the type (the Firebase table: all Gremlins, all Elephants), and in the data every upgrade is a tech whose effects target the unit type itself. So an added weapon is an acquired weapon and an added button (the Flamethrower's Flash Bang, the Wraith's Scorch, the Banshee's Boost, the Brutes' Jump Pack) an ability with source upgrade, both linking `upgrade-in-field` (Paired entries). Upgrades that only change numbers go in notes. Upgrade levels are not tiers (the tiers word list names Halo Wars for this).
  - The super upgrades swap a unit for a stronger one for one leader: Marines into ODSTs (Cutter), Scorpions into Grizzlies (Forge), Hornets into Hawks (Anders) (manual; Leader gameplay pages). If a super unit is coded, its price is the base unit's (cost_band.raw leaves out upgrades bought for every unit of the type) and its gate is the tech level its upgrade needs (the data: 3 for ODSTs, 4 for Grizzlies and Hawks).
  - Side-wide research stays off: the Field Armory's Adrenaline (faster infantry), Reserves (faster training) and Reinforcements (more population), the Temple's Forerunner Shield (faster shield recharge for every Covenant unit) and Followers, and the turret upgrades.
- **Leaders** (subfactions in the registry): each player picks one of three leaders for the side (manual, PDF pages 9 and 10, 17 and 18).
  - A UNSC leader never takes the field in skirmish: he or she brings a leader power, a unique unit, a super upgrade and an economy bonus. The economy bonuses stay off.
  - A Covenant leader is a hero on the field, placed for free when the first Temple is finished, one at a time, outside the population count, and bought again at the Temple for 400 after a death (Covenant Temple page; manual). Its powers (the Arbiter's Rage, the Chieftain's Vortex, the Prophet's Cleansing beam) cost supplies for every second they run (manual). They are the leader unit's own abilities: record them there, source innate, with the running cost in the summary.
- **UNSC leader powers** (side-wide; leave them off): picked from the radial menu of the orbiting ship (Leader power page). MAC Blast (Cutter), ODST Drop (Cutter, which drops new ODST squads where the player points: a call-in, like Red Alert's paratroopers, not a button of the ODSTs), Carpet Bomb (Forge), Cryo Bomb (Anders, which freezes units in place and makes frozen aircraft crash; Ellen Anders/Gameplay page), and for every UNSC leader Disruption Bomb (stops leader powers inside a zone for a while), Heal and Repair (restores units and mends buildings in an area, but not while they fight; its own page) and Pelican Transport (dropships lift a small group of units elsewhere). None gives a named unit type a new button, so no `hw1` ability has source commander-power. The Pelican and Covenant Spirit dropships in the data (role line Troop Transport) appear in no building's list in the manual or on Halopedia: not researched.
- **Covenant Gravity Lift** (no pattern): every Covenant base has one; units sent into it come out beside the leader, the Scarab excepted, and its menu can recall the leader for a fee (manual, PDF page 20; Covenant Citadel page). A base feature: leave it off.
- **Supply crates** (picking one up is the universal pick-up key): crates lie on the map at the start and are left by destroyed neutral bases; only infantry and scout units can collect them (manual, PDF page 8; Resources page; the Warthog's, Ghost's and Brute Chopper's manual entries say they can). Leave collecting off, and never code `gather-resources` for it: nobody carries anything back.
- **Garrisoning neutral structures** (`carry-passengers` on the structure, never on the riders): infantry can enter certain map structures and hold them. Sniper Towers are indestructible and make their occupants harder to kill and longer-reaching (Covenant watchtower page; Halo Nation's Standard page); Forerunner secondary reactors raise the holder's tech level by one, supply elevators feed it supplies, the lifesupport pod adds ten population, towers on Tundra and Fort Deen raise energy walls, on Tundra infantry can take over the Antlion mortar turret, and on Release the Relics let the holder unleash Flood waves that attack both sides (the pages of each, and the Emp'seam-pattern Antlion and Tundra pages). Halo Nation adds that garrisoning one costs a population slot; no other page read says so.
  - In the data the tactics files of most infantry carry in-cover copies of their weapons that reach much further (the Marines' rifle: 60 against 25), and the damage table has separate in-cover categories: that is this garrison effect. Never code the in-cover weapons; range bands use the weapon in the open, and the bonus goes in notes where it matters.
- **Transports** (no pattern for the game): no unit buildable in skirmish carries others. Armies move by Pelican Transport (UNSC power) and the Gravity Lift (Covenant base). Give no `hw1` unit passenger seats for them.
- **Spartans and vehicles** (not game-wide): the Spartan's Jack special takes an enemy vehicle (`hijack-vehicle`) and the same special on a friendly vehicle boards it to boost it (`join-ally-crew`). Only one Spartan per vehicle, and the Scarab, Vulture and Vampire cannot be taken (manual, Spartan and Vampire entries; Boarding page). Record both on the Spartan. The vehicles get no passenger seats for it; a vehicle that cannot be taken says so in its strengths.
- **Shields** (armour model `regen-shield` where the stock unit has one): Covenant shields recharge, and the Temple's Forerunner Shield speeds that up (Covenant Temple page; manual, PDF page 20). In the data only three of the units read have a shield as bought: the Spartan, the Locust and the Prophet of Regret. The Wraith's Heavy Shield, the Ghost's Scout Shield, the Elite Honor Guard's Personal Shield, the Jackal's Defense Gauntlet and the Hunter's Bonded Shield come with upgrades: put those in armour.notes (Stock values). The manual gives the Spartan an energy shield but no page read says it recharges (Halopedia's line saying so sits in a hidden comment of the Halo Wars page): check the Spartan's own page before coding `regen-shield`.
- **Repair and healing** (no pattern for the game): healing comes from Heal and Repair (UNSC power), from units that heal others (the Engineer; the Cyclops after its Repair Kit upgrade; the Medic a Marine squad gains with its third upgrade) and from Covenant shields recharging. No page read says units heal on their own: code self-repair only from a unit's own page. Units that heal others record it on themselves (`repair-allies`).
- **Population and caps** (no pattern): every unit uses population room (manual, PDF page 7). Spartans are capped at three and use none, and a Covenant leader is one at a time (manual): record those caps in availability and tier.basis on those units.
- **Fog of war** (no pattern): enemies show only near your own units and buildings; explored ground you no longer watch turns grey (manual, PDF page 6). Sight bands come from the data's LOS (see the registry's sight_reference).
- **Cloaking and detection** (not game-wide): only the Arbiter (Ghastly Vision, a permanent cloak) and the Elite Honor Guard (its Cloak upgrade) can cloak (Active camouflage page; Covenant Temple and Covenant Citadel pages). No page or data flag read names a detector: give no unit the detector trait unless its own page does.
- **Rams** (not game-wide): the Warthog's Ram, the Brute Chopper's Run Over and the Ghost's Boosted Ram (an upgrade) are those units' own specials (manual), sharing one ram damage category in the data. No page read says tanks run over infantry by themselves: give no unit `crush` from this note.
- **Stuns, freezing and EMP** (no pattern for the game): they come from named sources only (Cryo Bomb, the Gremlin's EMP, the Flash Bang upgrade, the Vampire's Stasis, the Brutes' Electric Shot upgrade, the Chieftain's hammer upgrades) and belong to them. The data marks which units each can touch (object types such as CanCryo, CanBeFlashBanged, EmpEffectNormal): use that in matchups, citing the data.
- **Base features** (leave off): base turrets and their add-ons, Covenant shield generators, the base lockdown and self-destruct of a fully upgraded base (Firebase and Covenant Citadel pages), recycling buildings, and sending supplies to an ally at a loss (Halo Nation's Supplies page).
- **Game modes and skulls** (leave off): bands use the Standard mode, in which players start with 800 supplies at tech level 0 (Halo Nation's Standard page). Deathmatch starts everything upgraded, and the Strategic Options modes (Keepaway, Tug of War, Reinforcements) change the rules of a match (Halo Nation's Deathmatch page; Halopedia's Strategic Options Pack page). Skulls found in the campaign can also be switched on in skirmish (Halo Wars page, Collectibles): leave them off.
- **Neutral units** (not researched): rebel infantry and snipers, Forerunner Sentinels and, on Release, the Flood guard or contest map structures, and some rebels start with veterancy (Rebel Infantry, Rebel base, Forerunner secondary reactor and Forerunner Relic pages). They are not sides: name them only in matchups.

No hw1 entry exists in data/games.json; this drafts the whole entry (validated against schemas/game.schema.json with the repository's ajv; its terms are in the word lists, its patterns in the registry, its id is new). Evidence for each part, paraphrased:

- id, title, kind, year, developer: https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars:_Definitive_Edition (infobox and lead) says the Definitive Edition remasters the 2009 Xbox 360 game, lists 343 Industries and Behaviour Interactive as its developers with Ensemble Studios for the original, and dates it 20 December 2016 (first as part of a Halo Wars 2 package, the Ultimate Edition) and 20 April 2017 (on its own). Franchise Halo as in hw2; control commanded, since the player gives orders to units (manual, PDF page 6, attacking and moving).
- version_researched: the Steam news feed of app 459220 holds five posts by 343 Industries from 21 April to 5 June 2017; every change listed is technical (runtime libraries, session browsing, the cursor, chat, leaderboards, per-AI difficulty, voice chat), e.g. https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/459220/view/1904307386970374726. https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_Title_Updates gives Title Update 2 (12 May 2009), 3 (17 July 2009) and 4 (18 December 2009) as balance updates and 5 (23 March 2011) as theater and server work only. The game data's update archive (techs_update.xml at the pinned address in sources) applies those balance changes as techs in every match (Anders, Prophet, Vampire, Warthog, turrets, Elephant, Gremlin, Scarab). Standard is the default skirmish mode and Deathmatch starts with everything upgraded (https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Standard_(Halo_Wars), https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Deathmatch_(Halo_Wars)).
- No expansions: the two DLC packs added three game modes (https://www.halopedia.org/Strategic_Options_Pack) and four maps (https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars, Historic Battle Map Pack list), and no units; both come with the Definitive Edition.
- factions: two playable sides, the UNSC and the Covenant, each with three leaders (manual, PDF pages 9, 10, 17 and 18; Halopedia's Halo Wars page, the leader table in Game concepts).
  - Leaders as subfactions, unlike the hw2 note: there are only six, fixed since 2009; each fields units the other two leaders of its side lack (the Firebase, Covenant Citadel and Covenant Factory tables: Elephant and ODSTs for Cutter, Cyclops and Grizzly for Forge, Gremlin and Hawk for Anders, Suicide Grunts for the Arbiter, Brutes and the Brute Chopper instead of the Ghost for the Brute Chieftain, the Elite Honor Guard for the Prophet), and the Covenant leaders are themselves units; the Chieftain's Grunt squads are led by a Brute where the other leaders' are led by an Elite (squads.xml; https://www.halopedia.org/HW:Brute_Chieftain, which also says his Chopper replaces the Ghost), a changed stock part that a subfaction entry can hold; Halopedia's Halo Wars page itself calls the leaders sub-factions, each bringing its own units and bonuses. This follows Red Alert 2's countries and Generals' generals, and the validator now lets a gate tagged with the parent serve a subfaction. Halo Wars 2 kept two factions because it has sixteen leaders who mostly swap one or two units. Alternative: two factions with leaders in notes, as hw2.
  - No Flood, rebel or Sentinel faction: on the multiplayer map Release, a Relic held by infantry releases Flood waves that attack both sides (https://www.halopedia.org/Forerunner_Relic), and rebels and Sentinels guard map structures (https://www.halopedia.org/Rebel_base, https://www.halopedia.org/Forerunner_secondary_reactor); none is a side a player commands.
  - flavour_affinity (a proposal): the Covenant's plasma weapons (the official site's Ghost, Banshee and Wraith entries at https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/Covenant), energy blades (the Arbiter and the Elite Honor Guard), hovering vehicles, Suicide Grunts and the Banshee's crash-on-death upgrade, and Engineers that mend fit empire's favoured plasma and blade families, hover movement and its kamikaze and repairing nano-tech themes (data/vocab/faction-flavours.json); its shields and cloaking lean allied, so it is a judgement call. The UNSC is mixed and left out, as hw2 did.
- has_tiers and tier_map: each unit, building and upgrade needs a tech level; UNSC reactors give one each (an Advanced Reactor two) up to four, the Covenant Temple gives one and its two Ages raise it to three, and a garrisoned Forerunner secondary reactor adds one (manual, PDF pages 13, 20 and the unit entries; https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Reactor; https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Temple; https://www.halopedia.org/Resources, which says the UNSC need 4 and the Covenant 3 to build everything); matches start at tech 0 (Halo Nation's Standard page). So the gate is the tech level. Bands by the tier word list: tech 0 needs no tech (t1); a level short of the side's top needs one or more tech steps (t2: UNSC 1 to 3, Covenant 1 and 2); the top level is top tech (t3: UNSC 4, Covenant 3, the Age of Reclamation). The Covenant leaders cost no tech in squads.xml but appear only once a Temple stands (Temple page), hence the Temple gate at t2. Only tech 3 and 4 differ by side, so only those carry a faction (a parent-tagged gate serves the leaders' subfactions; scripts/validate.mjs). With the levels from squads.xml, t1 holds Marines, Flamethrowers, the Warthog, Elephant, Grunts, Jackals, Ghost, Brute Chopper and Engineer; t2 the Spartan, Cyclops, Gremlin, Scorpion, Hornet, Cobra, Wolverine, Hunters, Wraith, Banshee, Brutes, Elite Honor Guard, Suicide Grunts, Locust, Vampire and the leaders; t3 the Vulture and the Scarab (and the Grizzly and Hawk super units, whose upgrades need tech 4 in techs.xml). Alternative: UNSC tech 3 (the Cobra and Wolverine) as t3.
- has_costs and cost_thresholds: supplies are the money; tech and population are passive requirements (Resources page; manual, PDF page 8). The two main battle tanks, both with the role line Main Vehicle: Scorpion 500 (https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Vehicle_Depot; squads.xml) and Wraith 350 (https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Factory; https://www.halopedia.org/Type-25_Wraith; squads.xml). Mean 425, so 212.5, 382.5, 595 and 850, rounded to 210, 380, 600 and 850. Bands of the data prices: very low: Marines, Flamethrowers, ODSTs, Grunts, Jackals and Ghost 100, Cyclops and Elite Honor Guard 125, Warthog and Brutes 150, Suicide Grunts 160, Gremlin, Banshee and Brute Chopper 200; low: Hornet, Hawk, Hunters, Engineer and Vampire 250, Spartan, Wolverine and Locust 300, Cobra and Wraith 350; medium: Elephant and the Covenant leaders 400, Scorpion and Grizzly 500; high: none; very high: Vulture 900, Scarab 3,000.
- speed_reference: objects.xml gives each Marine Velocity 10; neither the manual nor Halopedia gives a speed. Engine check: not possible from the sources; the field sits beside Acceleration and TurnRate, and Grunt bodies carry the same 10 and acceleration while the manual (PDF page 21) and their rollover text call them slow, so a squad's real pace is unproven. Sample ratios: Scorpion and Wraith 2.0, Warthog and Ghost 4.0, Hornet 3.0, Vulture 1.2, Scarab 1.5, Elephant 0.9.
- sight_reference: objects.xml gives the Marines LOS 55; the manual (PDF page 6) says enemies are seen only near your own units and buildings; the units read range from 55 to 80.
- range_reference: unsc_inf_marine_01.tactics gives the assault rifle 25 and its in-cover copy 60; Halo Nation's Standard page says Sniper Towers and cover make garrisoned units reach further and resist damage, which is what the in-cover copies are.
- damage_map: weapontypes.xml defines seventeen weapon types with a multiplier against each target category, and each weapon's type is in its unit's tactics file. Mapped: Fire (the Flamethrower) to fire; ArmorPiercing (the Cobra's railguns, the Gremlin's cannon), FuelRod (the Hunters), BansheeFuelRod and Missile (the Hornet's rockets; all tripled or nearly so against Medium and Heavy) to armour-piercing; AntiAir (the Wolverine, Vampire and Vulture missiles), Explosive (the Scorpion's cannon, the Wraith's mortar, both with area), Grenade (grenades, rockets, grenade launchers) and BruteShot to explosive; Beam (the Locust) to energy; AntiInfantry (the Jackal's carbine and rifle) and GaussCannon (the Warthog's upgrade) to kinetic. Left out: SmallArms and AASmallArms (shared by rifles, plasma pistols and cannons, an SMG and the Elite Honor Guard's sword), Basic and LeaderPower (generic), WarthogRam (the rams).
- armour_map: objects.xml gives each body a DamageType, the target category the damage table reads (damagetypes.xml lists them). The table shows the categories' toughness: small arms do more than full damage to Light, LightArmored and Medium and well under full to Heavy; anti-air weapons triple against MediumAir. Mapped: Light (basic infantry) to unarmoured, LightArmored and CovenantLeader (armoured soldiers and the two melee leaders) to light, Medium (light vehicles and the Cobra and Wolverine) to medium, MediumAir (all five aircraft) to light, Heavy (the Scorpion, Grizzly, Elephant and Scarab) to heavy; the notes step the Warthog, Gremlin and Brute Chopper down to light (the manual calls the first two lightly armoured). Shielded, Building, Flood and the in-cover categories are left out.
- scope added and added_reason: docs/proposal.md, section 2.2, says Halo Wars is new to the research and R4's prep adds its registry entry (plan change of 24 October 2026).
- teaches_patterns: the Spartan's Jack special takes enemy vehicles and boards friendly ones to boost them (manual, PDF page 15; https://www.halopedia.org/Boarding_(gameplay_mechanic)): hijack-vehicle and join-ally-crew (join-ally-crew's file already lists Halo Wars' Spartans as an example, and hijack-vehicle's reaches the same mechanic through its Halo Wars 2 example). The Cobra locks down into an artillery mode good against buildings (manual, PDF page 16): deploy-siege-mode, whose file cites the Halo Wars Cobra. The Elephant locks down to train infantry in the field (manual, PDF page 16): host-spawn-point. The Gremlin's EMP disables vehicles for a time (manual, PDF page 16): disable-machine.
- status planned: no batch has coded its units.

notes.other_notes:
- **Version.** Research the Definitive Edition (2016 bundle, Steam and Windows from 20 April 2017). Its five patches (21 April to 5 June 2017, posted by 343 Industries on Steam) are all technical: no balance change. Its game data keeps the Xbox 360 game's balance after Title Updates 2 to 4: the update archive applies them as balance techs (Anders, Prophet, Vampire, Warthog, turrets, Elephant, Gremlin, Scarab), matching Halopedia's Halo Wars Title Updates page. Title Update 4 (18 December 2009) was the last balance change; Title Update 5 (23 March 2011) only fixed theater playback and server links. Use Standard-mode values (Deathmatch starts fully upgraded).
- **Sites to cite, one page each for the plant test** (run `npm run plant-test -- <address>` before any fill):
  - www.halopedia.org (passed on 11 November on another page): https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Vehicle_Depot. Read through https://www.halopedia.org/api.php with prop=wikitext|text. The Halo Wars building tables use templates (HWResources, HWTech, HWPop) whose icons the rendered page shows: the figure is the number after the icon.
  - halo.fandom.com, Halo Nation (passed on 11 November on another page): https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Standard_(Halo_Wars). Read through https://halo.fandom.com/api.php.
  - raw.githubusercontent.com, the Definitive Edition's game data (new for R4; must be tested): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coconutbird/ensemble-assets/1e8ced921a6dd099c4eac0936aa2f737c5d84ae6/save/root.era/data/tactics/unsc_inf_marine_01.tactics.xml.
  - store.steampowered.com, single news posts of app 459220 (the copy-check reads single posts; test one): https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/459220/view/1904307386970374726.
  - halo.wiki.gallery, Halopedia's copies of the two official PDFs (the manual, https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/4/4d/HW_Manual.pdf, and the quick reference chart, https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/9/91/HW_TechTree.pdf). The copy-check cannot read a PDF: check paraphrases of them by hand (`pdftotext`, then a six-word check). The manual's two-column layout comes out mixed up with `pdftotext -layout`; plain `pdftotext` keeps the reading order.
  - liquipedia.net is not used for Halo Wars: nothing is requested from it.
- **The game data** (cite as kind database, title naming the file and saying it is the Definitive Edition's data copied in the ensemble-assets repository). It is a public copy of the retail files (`root.era`, with `root_update.era` on top), saved by a third-party project that loads the game's data (ensemble-assets). Use the pinned commit above in every address, so a cited page cannot change. The files:
  - `save/root.era/data/objects.xml` (one entry per unit body: `Velocity`, `LOS`, `DamageType` (the armour category), `Hitpoints`, `Shieldpoints`, `Pop`, `Veterancy`, its `Tactics` file);
  - `save/root.era/data/squads.xml` (one entry per thing you buy: price in `Supplies`, the tech level it needs as a `Power` cost, the bodies in it, `RoleTextID`);
  - `save/root.era/data/tactics/<object>.tactics.xml` (weapons with `WeaponType`, `MaxRange`, damage, area; actions). File names are lower case (flamemarine and brutechopper in place of flameMarine and bruteChopper), while the object names keep capitals;
  - `save/root_update.era/data/weapontypes.xml` (the damage table) and `save/root.era/data/damagetypes.xml` (the target categories);
  - `save/root.era/data/techs.xml` and `save/root_update.era/data/techs_update.xml` (upgrades, and the Title Update balance techs). A unit's figure can be changed by a balance tech there (the Gremlin's tech level is): check `techs_update.xml` for the unit before banding.
  - Object names for the common units all end in `_01`. UNSC infantry starts with `unsc_inf_`: marine, flameMarine, spartan, cyclops and odst. UNSC vehicles start with `unsc_veh_`: warthog, elephant, gremlin, scorpion, grizzly, cobra and wolverine. UNSC aircraft start with `unsc_air_`: hornet, hawk and vulture. Covenant infantry starts with `cov_inf_`: grunt (an Elite leads the squad: eliteLeader; the Chieftain's squads are bruteGrunt), jackal, hunter, brute, eliteCommando (the Elite Honor Guard), suicideGrunt, engineer, arbiter, bruteChief and prophet. Covenant vehicles start with `cov_veh_`: ghost, bruteChopper, wraith, locust and scarab. Covenant aircraft start with `cov_air_`: banshee and vampire. So the Marine squad's object is `unsc_inf_marine_01`.
- **Reading cost.** objects.xml (about 1.4 MB) and techs.xml (about 0.4 MB) are too big to read whole: search them for the unit's object name and read that entry only. A unit's tactics file is a few kilobytes. With the building table, the manual entry and the data entries, a unit should need four or five pages (an estimate, not measured).
- **When the data and a wiki disagree,** follow the data for the version researched and add an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree that names the wiki page (the rule R1 set for Red Alert's rules copy). Known cases: the Brute Chopper costs 200 in the data and 100 on Halopedia's Covenant Factory table; the Engineer needs no tech level in the data, the manual and the chart, but 1 on the Covenant Summit table; the Cobra needs tech 3 in the data, the manual, the chart and the Vehicle Depot table, but 2 on Halopedia's SP42 Cobra page; the Grizzly upgrade needs tech 4 in the data and on the John Forge/Gameplay page, but 3 on the Vehicle Depot table; a Marine squad has four soldiers in the data, five on the official site's page; the official site arms the Spartan with a rifle, the data gives it an SMG. Official text written in 2009 still decides role words and matchups.
- **Grunt speed.** Grunts move exactly as fast as Marines in the data (same `Velocity` and acceleration), but the manual and the rollover text call them slow. Band from the data figure and add an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree. Nothing read shows whether a squad moves at its bodies' `Velocity` in the engine; the engine itself was not checked.
- **Figures in the data.** Speed: `Velocity` divided by the Marines' 10 (speed_raw). Sight: every unit read has an LOS from 55 to 80, so every sight band is medium (the Marines' 55 is the reference; long needs more than 82.5), and scout can never rest on long sight. Range: the reference is the Marines' rifle, 25; ignore the in-cover weapons (garrison only). Many vehicle weapons reach past their own unit's LOS (the Scorpion's cannon reaches 65 with LOS 55; the Wraith's mortar 70; machine guns of 60 on several vehicles), so range bands will often say off-screen by the rule's first reason. Code it as the rule says and report it as a rule problem if it looks wrong.
- **Squads.** Body counts come from `squads.xml`: Marines 4 (New Blood adds one, the Medic another), Flamethrowers 2, Jackals 2, Hunters 2 (a bonded pair), Brutes 2, Suicide Grunts 4, Grunt squads 1 leader and 3 Grunts (Peons adds one more, although the manual says two). Each body has its own `Pop`; a squad's population is their sum.
- **Weapons in the data.** One tactics file holds every weapon a unit can use, those its upgrades and specials unlock included. A weapon listed there can be switched off until an upgrade turns it on (an ActionEnable effect in techs.xml): the Warthog's machine gun waits for Gunner and the Brute Chopper's plasma cannon for Autocannons, so both start armed only with their ram (the official site and the HW:Brute Chieftain page say the same). Check techs.xml before coding a listed weapon as stock. The Y special is usually its own weapon there (the Marines' Grenade, the Scorpion's canister shell, the Vulture's barrage, the Gremlin's EMP): it is an ability, not a weapon (Weapons vs abilities). Upgrade weapons (the Warthog's machine gun and Gauss cannon, the Hornet's Wingmen, the Jackal's beam rifle) are acquired weapons. A weapon's `TargetPriority` list hints at what it engages (the Scorpion's machine gun lists flying units, its cannon does not), but no page says it is the full list of what it can hit: use it as support, beside a page.
- **Halopedia pages for units.** Halopedia's Halo Wars facts on a unit are spread over the In-game information sections of lore pages (M808B Scorpion, SP42 Cobra, Type-25 Wraith) and some Gameplay subpages that cover several games (Sangheili Honor Guardsman/Gameplay, Type-26 Banshee/Gameplay, Kig-Yar/Gameplay); many units have little there. The building tables (the pages under Official role lines) are the best per-unit source; the leader pages are James Cutter/Gameplay, John Forge/Gameplay, Ellen Anders/Gameplay, The Arbiter (leader) and HW:Brute Chieftain. Some Halopedia text sits in hidden comments, which readers do not see: the Halo Wars page's old unit list (the Spartan's shield and SMGs, the Flood on Release) is one. Read the rendered text, and never rest a code on commented-out text.
- **Leaders as subfactions.** The registry entry lists the six leaders as subfactions with parent unsc or covenant. A unit every leader of a side fields belongs to the side. A unit only some leaders field belongs to the most general faction that fields it; when two of three do (the Ghost: Arbiter and Prophet, while the Chieftain fields the Brute Chopper instead), record it under the side and say in tier.basis which leader lacks it (the rule R1 used for Red Alert 2's Attack Dog). A leader's changed version of a side's unit (the Chieftain's Brute-led Grunt squad) is its own entry under that leader with variant_of, if the trim keeps it.
- **Armour map steps** (armour-class step 1 lets these notes name a step): the Warthog, the Gremlin and the Brute Chopper take one step down from the map's medium to light. The manual calls the Warthog lightly armoured and the Gremlin light armoured, the Chopper is a bike (our light class names motorbikes), and in the data all three have well under half the Cobra's health. Shielded is left out of the map because the data gives it to infantry, vehicles and a leader alike, with no shield on some of them as bought (the Wraith, the Ghost, the Elite Honor Guard): those units go on to steps 2 to 5 (the Wraith, a cost-anchor tank, is heavy by step 3).
- **Flood, rebels and Sentinels** are map neutrals, not sides: no faction for them.
- **Flavour.** The Covenant gets empire as a judgement call (plasma weapons, energy blades, hovering vehicles, Suicide Grunts and the Banshee's crash attack, Engineers that mend); its shields and cloaking lean allied. The UNSC is left out as mixed, as in Halo Wars 2.
- **Patterns to look for**, beyond the registry entry's teaches_patterns: `self-destruct` (Suicide Grunts; the Banshee's Sacrifice upgrade), `pull-target` (the Chieftain's Birthright upgrade and Vortex), `retaliate-on-hit` (the Arbiter's Fiendish Return), `overclock-self` (the Arbiter's Rage, paid in supplies per second), `bombard-area` (the Prophet's Cleansing beam), `repair-allies` (the Engineer; the Cyclops after its Repair Kit), `cloak` (the Elite Honor Guard), `leap` (the Brutes' Jump Pack), `lock-in-stasis` or `disable-machine` for the Vampire's Stasis (it holds aircraft and, with its upgrade, drains them, so check which summary fits), `leave-hazard-zone` (the Wraith's Scorch), the Hornet's Chaff Pod (a passive upgrade that turns missiles aside: weigh `fire-countermeasures`, which is on a key, against the interceptor armour model, which works by itself) and `launch-drones` (the Prophet's two Protector Sentinels, an upgrade).
- **Choices that need a look** (the editor's or Mustafa's): leaders as subfactions rather than notes as in Halo Wars 2; the game data from a third-party copy of the retail files as a database source for speed, sight, range, prices and the two maps; UNSC tech level 3 at t2 rather than t3; the Covenant's empire flavour.

missing: Official site wording that the role notes do not list, all on https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/UNSC and /Covenant (official text by the note's own rule): the Scorpion's main gun is said to struggle against some heavily armoured vehicles (a weak point naming armour, which drops anti-armour from its secondary roles) and its header calls it a Main Battle Artillery Tank (a siege alias, a trap at roles.secondary step 1); the Vulture is said to be built to deal heavy damage to enemy ground troops (strong-against infantry, not 'nothing') and to be exposed to anti-air fire and enemy aircraft because it is slow (a weak point naming air); the Hornet is called a flexible anti-air unit (anti-air label); the Ghost is called a scout vehicle that is good at harrying infantry (strong-against infantry, and a raider alias in word form); the Banshee is used for scouting and harassment and hurts ground and air forces alike; Jackals often serve as scouts or snipers (scout and marksman aliases); Hunters fill a strong anti-vehicle role; the Vampire is the core Covenant anti-air craft and the Wolverine an anti-air vehicle; the Wraith carries anti-personnel plasma cannons. Also: the Cobra's manual entry (PDF page 16) and rollover call its deployed form artillery that is good against buildings (siege alias), and the Gremlin's rollover says it does well against enemy ground vehicles (strong-against armour) besides its infantry weakness (Firebase table).

Vampire boarding: the game data disagrees with the manual. objects.xml gives the type SpartanBoardFlying to cov_air_vampire_01 as to the Banshee, Hornet and Hawk (no tech removes it), and the Spartan's tactics file has an AircraftTakeOver action, while the manual's Vampire entry (PDF page 23) says Spartans cannot jack it. Add it to the known disagreement cases (official text vs data).

Hawk super upgrade tech level: 4 in techs.xml (unsc_hawk_upgrade1, Power 4), on the chart (sheet 1) and on https://www.halopedia.org/Ellen_Anders/Gameplay, but 3 on the UNSC Airpad table, like the Grizzly case the note lists. The Airpad price of 1,350 is Anders' halved upgrade cost raised by half in Title Update 2 (techs_update.xml unsc_LeaderAnders_balance; Halo_Wars_Title_Updates), against 1,800 in techs.xml.

Population pools: leaders.xml (pinned commit, root.era/data/leaders.xml) gives separate pools: Unit (30 for UNSC leaders, 40 for Covenant, max 99), Spartan (max 3), Leader (max 1) and Temple (max 1). objects.xml still gives the Spartan and the three leaders Pop 1, so the note's rule that a squad's population is the sum of its bodies' Pop must not charge Spartans or leaders unit population.

Super units in squads.xml point at the base unit's bodies: the ODST squad lists four unsc_inf_marine_01 plus a Marine and a Medic, the Hawk squad the Hornet body and the Grizzly squad the Scorpion body; the super upgrade techs swap them with TransformProtoUnit and TransformProtoSquad (techs.xml unsc_odst_upgrade1, unsc_hawk_upgrade1, unsc_grizzly_upgrade1). Coders must read the super unit's own object (unsc_inf_odst_01 for the ODST, and the Hawk's and the Grizzly's in the same way), not the squad's body list. Related trap: the Hawk's laser has WeaponType Missile (unsc_air_hawk_01.tactics), so the damage map makes it armour-piercing.

The Covenant Engineer flies in the data: cov_inf_engineer_01 has MovementType Air and the object types Aircraft and Flying, and the manual's Summit (an aircraft building) trains it (PDF page 20). Its DamageType is Light, so the note's reading 'Light means infantry' and the armour map's Light to unarmoured meet a flying unit here; the Engineer also cannot repair itself (Archive:Halowars.com/Covenant, Engineer).

candidates.name: Spartan
candidates.role_guess: infiltrator (steals vehicles), with assault, and buffer for the friendly vehicle it drives
candidates.teaches: A super-soldier with a recharging shield who swaps bodies in mid-fight. It takes over enemy vehicles, and it can also take the controls of a friendly vehicle, which then gets about 15% more defence and damage (more with each Spartan upgrade) and a far higher veterancy cap (13 or 14 points instead of the usual 3). Only three per army, and they sit outside the population cap. Iconic counter: it beats vehicles by stealing them.

candidates.shooter_note: A tough soldier whose big play is boarding: jump into an enemy tank to take it, or into a teammate's tank to make it stronger.

candidates.name: Elephant
candidates.teaches: A mobile mini-base: an armoured troop carrier that has to deploy before it can train infantry (Marines, Hellbringers, Spartans) in the field. Its turret upgrade works only while it is deployed. In a Renegade-style shooter it becomes the forward spawn and buy point that the enemy must hunt down; the twist is that it is only useful once parked.

candidates.repeats: host-spawn-point is coded on Tempest Rising's Vimana, and the registry notes name the PlanetSide 2 Sunderer as an example. Deploying in order to work is like Yuri's Slave Miner. produce-unit-in-field is the other possible reading. Halo Wars 2 has no Elephant: its page has only a Halo Wars section.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow armoured truck that carries a squad forward, then plants itself as a spawn and buy point, with a gun that works only while planted.

candidates.name: Arbiter
candidates.teaches: A hero with twin energy swords. His Rage mode puts the player in direct control: the view follows him, the sticks move him and swing his swords, and he can leap onto targets he picks. Rage costs the team resources for every second it runs. Upgrades heal him for each kill made in Rage, make Rage cheaper, raise the attack of allies near him, send part of the damage he takes back at the attacker, and in the end keep him cloaked for good. He can reach aircraft only in Rage. The twist is a power mode that eats the team's money by the second.

new_mechanics.summary: An ability that keeps running only while the team's shared money pays for it every second, so using it trades the team's economy for power (the Arbiter's Rage and the Prophet's Cleansing Beam). It may fit better as a new resource term than as a pattern.

candidates.repeats: overclock-self as on Red Alert 3's Kirov and Tempest Rising's Voltaic Tank, but paid in team money. cloak as on Jarmen Kell. rally-allies as on the Line Officer. retaliate-on-hit as on the Thunderhead, here as reflected damage, with the range not stated. candidates.shooter_note: A sword duellist with a berserk mode that drains the team's credits every second: strong, but a money sink, and unable to hit aircraft outside that mode.

candidates.name: Prophet of Regret
candidates.teaches: A hero on an anti-gravity throne. He fires plasma cannons (fuel rod cannons with an upgrade), two Protector Sentinels float beside him once bought, and a last upgrade turns him into a true air unit. His Cleansing power calls down a beam from an orbiting ship, and the player steers it by stick anywhere within his sight. The beam burns every unit under it, his own side included, but never him; it uses supplies, and its upgrades cut that cost. Counter: once he flies, a Vampire's stasis stops both his attacks and his beam.

new_mechanics.summary: Call a beam down from above and steer it by hand over ground you can see. It burns everything beneath it while you keep it up, your own side included, but never you.

An ability that keeps running only while the team's shared money pays for it, so using it trades the team's economy for power (shared with the Arbiter's Rage). It may fit better as a resource term than as a pattern.

candidates.teaches: A hero with a gravity hammer, built to wreck heavy vehicles. Upgrades add a stun to his blows, let a charged swing drag enemies to him, and widen the stun to an area; the Temple table also has him kill stunned infantry outright. His Vortex power raises a spinning vortex that shreds everything near it and blows up when he ends it, and later upgrades let it draw in more enemies. Counter detail: the vortex is his only way to hit aircraft.

new_mechanics.summary: Hold up a vortex or field that pulls in and grinds enemies; ending it, or having it cut short, sets off a final blast, so the skill is in timing the release.

It is weak against ground targets, so it needs an escort.

The counter is built in: kill one and the other gets much easier.

new_mechanics.summary: Two units fielded as a bonded pair hit much harder while both are alive; when one dies, the survivor loses the bonus and becomes easier prey. band-together is the nearest id, but it counts nearby group members rather than one named partner.

candidates.coverage_note:
There are 15 candidates, in my order of preference. Numbers 1 to 10 teach the most; the Cobra, Ghost, Cyclops, Jackal and Scarab are spares for the judge.

Classes: infantry 5 (Spartan, Arbiter, Brute Chieftain, Hunter, Jackal), vehicle 3 (Elephant, Gremlin, Cobra), walker 3 (Locust, Cyclops, Scarab), hover 2 (Prophet of Regret on his anti-gravity throne, Ghost), aircraft 2 (Vampire, Banshee). Halo Wars has no buildable drone or ship; the Prophet's two Protector escorts come with an upgrade.

Factions: UNSC 5, Covenant 10, on purpose. Most UNSC lines carry on into Halo Wars 2 (Marines, Hellbringers, ODSTs, Warthog, Scorpion, Grizzly, Wolverine, Hornet, Vulture, Spartans, Cyclops). So the UNSC list keeps the units only Halo Wars has (Elephant, Gremlin, Cobra), plus the two shared lines whose Halo Wars versions differ (Spartan, Cyclops). The Covenant faction exists only in Halo Wars, and its three leaders fight on the field as heroes.

Leader-locked units: Elephant (Cutter), Cyclops (Forge), Gremlin (Anders), each Covenant leader, and the Ghost (not available to the Chieftain). Unit ids follow the hw2 precedent: factions unsc and covenant, with the leader named in notes. They change if the hw1 registry entry, which does not exist yet in data/games.json, adds leader subfactions.

Roles: every role except area-denial and logistics.

Prices are compressed. Jackal and Ghost cost 100, Cyclops 125, Gremlin and Banshee 200, Hunter and Vampire 250, Spartan and Locust 300, Cobra 350, the Elephant and each leader 400, and the Scarab 3,000. The two main battle tanks are the Scorpion at 500 and the Wraith at 350. So the price bands depend on the anchor the registry entry picks. Only the Scarab, and the Vulture (900, left out), sit far above the rest.
